newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Turkey asks for security after Kurd protest at UN.
newsitem.headline: Turkey asks for security after Kurd protest at UN.

text.p: Turkey asked the United Nations on Thursday to reinforce security at its European headquarters in Geneva after 200 Kurdish protesters rushed past guards at the gate and occupied part of the sprawling complex last week.
Turkey's ambassador to the world body in Geneva, Tugay Ulucevik, said Ankara demanded concrete measures to avoid similar incidents in the future.
Ulucevik, who took the floor at a U.N. disarmament meeting at the Palais des Nations, said Turkey deplored what he called "impunity" towards the Kurds involved, saying they had yet to be punished.
The non-violent demonstration a week ago, in protest at Turkey's offensive into northern Iraq, was the first of its kind inside the building in the U.N.'s history in Geneva.

The Turkish Kurd demonstrators chanted slogans in support of Kurdish independence, brandished red, yellow and green PKK flags and banners and danced. They left after three hours of negotiations with U.N. officials.
Swiss police said they could not intervene without a formal request from U.N. officials but a riot squad was on standby.
